passage:
I'm Nazia, and it took me a whole semester to see the pattern. Bidisha called at odd hours: the night before submissions for my notes, before a trip for my cousin's contact at a travel agency, on the fifteenth for a small loan. When I had nothing to give, her messages went quiet. I said yes every time because I was scared she'd stop liking me, and I even bought her coffee to keep things warm.

One evening I noticed I felt used, and also that I still cared about her. So I did something small. "I'll share my notes today, but I can't do it every time. And I'd love to just hang out sometime with no favours." She looked surprised. "Oh. I didn't realise." We're not as close as before, but I help when I want to, and it feels cleaner.

qa.q: What did Bidisha ask for before a trip?
qa.a: Nazia's cousin's contact at a travel agency.

qa.q: Why did Nazia keep saying yes at first?
qa.a: Out of fear that Bidisha would stop liking Nazia, so Nazia even bought coffee to keep things warm.

qa.q: What limit did Nazia set, and how did it help?
qa.a: Nazia offered notes that day, said it could not be every time, and invited a no-favours hangout. It was clear without bitterness.

qa.q: How might Bidisha have seen the pattern?
qa.a: Possibly without noticing it. Bidisha's "Oh. I didn't realise" suggests surprise rather than deliberate use.

grounding: Nazia realises a friend calls only when she needs something, and sets limits without bitterness.

passage:
Wednesday
Samir called today. First time in five weeks. "Bhai, how are you, long time!" and then, within a minute, "Can you send your Thermodynamics notes? And your cousin's number, the one at the placement cell?"
I sent the notes. I always do. And then I sat there feeling stupid, because I realised I can't remember the last time he called just to talk. Every call comes with a list.
I used to think if I helped enough, he'd start seeing me as a real friend. Tonight that idea felt kind of sad.
So when he messaged "and the cousin's number?", I wrote: "I'd rather not pass on family numbers. Notes, happy to share. And call sometime just to talk, yaar, I'd like that."
He sent a thumbs up. Maybe he'll call. Maybe not. Either way, I'm not buying anyone's company with my cousin's number.
— Ojas

qa.q: What did Samir ask for besides the notes?
qa.a: The number of Ojas's cousin at the placement cell.

qa.q: How did Ojas feel after sending the notes?
qa.a: Stupid and a little sad, realising Samir never calls just to talk.

qa.q: What limit did Ojas set, and why was it a healthy one?
qa.a: Ojas kept sharing notes but declined to pass on the cousin's number and asked Samir to call just to talk; it was a limit without bitterness.

qa.q: How might Samir see Ojas's reply?
qa.a: Possibly surprised and a little embarrassed; the thumbs up suggests he got the message without a fight.

grounding: Shows realising a friend only calls when they need something, and helping by choice while setting limits instead of buying affection.

subtype: Friend × Being used for notes, money or contacts [Receiver]
passage:
Uday's phone lit up during his lunch break at the bank. It was the third favour since March, and the only kind of message Ankita ever sent.
Ankita: heyyy uday 🙂 long time!!
Ankita: quick favour, can you refer my cousin for the analyst opening at your office?
Uday: hi ankita
Uday: last time i referred your friend, she didn't turn up for the interview. my manager asked me about it
Ankita: oh no, i didn't know 😅
Uday: it's ok. but i can only refer people i know
Uday: if your cousin wants, i can share the job link and tell her what the interviews are like
Ankita: that's fair, sorry
Ankita: also... we should actually meet sometime, not just when i need stuff
Uday: haha i was going to say that
Uday: coffee on saturday? no favours allowed
Ankita: deal ☕

qa.a: To refer her cousin for the analyst opening at Uday's office.

qa.q: What does Uday's flat "hi ankita" suggest about how he feels?
qa.a: He feels tired and a little used, having noticed that Ankita only messages when she needs a favour.

qa.q: How did Uday set a limit without bitterness?
qa.a: He explained he could only refer people he knew, offered the job link and interview tips instead, and suggested coffee with no favours allowed.

qa.q: How does Ankita respond to the limit?
qa.a: She apologises, calls it fair, and admits they should meet not only when she needs something.

grounding: Illustrates being used by a friend for contacts and setting a clear limit without bitterness rather than giving more to win affection.
